paragraphs: Halfway up the hill, Yellow Duck Sweater noticed the hill was made of pancakes. Not flat ones: thick, warm, slightly springy ones, stacked at a slope of exactly one and a half metres, and every step sank its orange feet in up to the toes. Butter ran downhill in slow gold rivers. The duck respected the hill, so it did not complain, but it did count. Reward for each step: one. Reward for each step that slid back: zero, and a small, private quack. Above the summit hung the moon, cut perfectly in half, its straight edge so clean it looked freshly sliced.

At the top it found two copies of itself already there, sitting on the last pancake with flour on their sweaters, heads tilted up, waiting the way checkpoints wait to be chosen. Slowly the half moon leaned down, as if it were curious, until its flat edge touched the summit like a ramp. It was cool and faintly powdery underfoot. The three of them stepped on, one behind the other, and the moon began to rise. Far below, the hill shrank to a coin, and the duck saw that its whole long climb had left a trail of small footprints in the butter, winding up and up like a row of knitted stitches.

imagePrompt: Yellow Duck Sweater, a small two-legged tabletop robot. Its head is a smooth, chunky white plastic shell shaped like a small loaf of bread: about one and a half times as long front to back as it is tall, deep and boxy with softly rounded corners and a mostly flat top. It is not a round dome or ball, and not a long thin tube. It has an orange trim along the bottom edge and a small orange hinge on each side. At the front of the head is a single round camera eye: a black lens inside a thick orange-yellow ring. It has no beak and no mouth. The head sits on a tall, thin neck, about as tall as the head is long, made of stacked black servo motors with a few loose black wires, leaning slightly forward. Its body is a small, boxy white torso with rounded corners. It has no arms and no hands. Its short legs are black servo joints with white plastic covers on the hips, knees slightly bent. Its feet are flat and rounded like duck feet, orange on top with yellow soles. It wears a small, chunky-knit, bright lemon-yellow crewneck sweater over its white torso, slightly too big, with a ribbed collar, cuffs, and hem. Knitted into the front of the sweater is a simple cartoon duckling: pale yellow body with a thick black outline, a black dot eye, a curved line for its wing, an orange beak, and orange feet. A single full-color comic page with six panels of equal size in a grid of two columns and three rows, separated by clean white gutters, read left to right and top to bottom. The same robot duck appears in every panel and looks identical each time, unless a panel says otherwise. No speech bubbles, captions, sound effects, panel numbers, or any other text. Panel 1: The robot duck walks up a steep hill made of a tall stack of thick golden pancakes, its orange feet sinking into the soft top layer, with rivers of melted butter running downhill. Panel 2: The robot duck slips back a little on the buttery pancake slope, leaning forward with its neck stretched toward the summit, while a half moon hangs in the night sky above. Panel 3: A close view of the robot duck's orange feet pressed into a pancake, leaving small footprints in the butter, with the half moon glowing beyond the hilltop. Panel 4: On the summit, three ducks, the robot duck and two identical copies all in yellow sweaters dusted with flour, sit on the top pancake with their heads tilted up toward the half moon. Panel 5: The half moon leans down from the sky until its flat straight edge rests on the summit like a ramp, and three ducks step onto it one behind the other. Panel 6: Three ducks ride the half moon high into the starry sky while, far below, the pancake hill looks as small as a coin, with a winding trail of tiny footprints climbing it. Warm children's comic art: clean confident ink outlines, soft flat colors with gentle shading, a dreamy night palette, cozy and a little surreal. Friendly for an 11-year-old. No text, letters, logos, or numbers anywhere in the image. Real people do not appear.
